summary: A scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Draszczyk earned her Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna (~2006–2012), also working there as a researcher around 2008. She studied under Lambert Schmithausen, David Seyfort Ruegg, Klaus-Dieter Mathes, and traditional teachers.
Specializing in Indology, Kropman studied as a PhD researcher at the University of Groningen in 2008 and succeeded Nina Mirnig.

Dibeltulo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~2008–2015) under doctoral supervisor Donald S. Lopez Jr., committee member Micah L. Auerback, and mentor Ester Bianchi.
A Buddhist studies scholar, Ujiie was an overseas research student at Tribhuvan University in 1970 and served as a lecturer at Koyasan University.

A historian and archaeologist, Eisenberg studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1939–1943) and Princeton University (~1946–1954). He held a post at the University of Michigan (~1949–1989), where he taught Leela Aditi Wood.

Specializing in Sinology and Buddhist studies, Cartelli completed her PhD at Columbia University by 1999 under doctoral supervisor Philip B. Yampolsky and committee members Irene Bloom, Robert P. Hymes, Victor H. Mair, Marsha Wagner, and Pei-yi Wu.

Wright was a historian and Sinologist who studied at Ramsay High School, Vassar College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University (~1939–1951). She held a post at Yale University from around 1959 to 1970.
Jaksch specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied at the University of Sunderland as a student of Peter Harvey.
Specializing in religious and Buddhist studies, White completed a double major honors degree at York University and pursued doctoral studies at Wilfrid Laurier University.

Rhie, a scholar in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Sinology, studied under mentors Harrie Vanderstappen and Pramod Chandra (~1965–1970). She served as a professor at Smith College from around 1974 to 2012.

A scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, Chikusa studied at Kyoto University (~1948–1953). He later held posts at Otani University (~1993–2000) and Kyoto University, becoming professor emeritus (~1993–2015).
Specializing in Indology and Buddhist studies, Enomoto studied under Jien Abe and served as an assistant professor at Kacho Junior College.

A scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Hattori studied at Kyoto and Calcutta universities. He held posts at Kyoto University (1955–1988), Osaka Gakuin University, Osaka Prefecture University, and visiting roles at Berkeley, Toronto, and Vienna.

A Buddhist studies scholar, Nitta completed doctoral credits at the University of Tokyo (~1961–1966). He served as a professor at Fukui Prefectural College (~1976–1992) and Fukui Prefectural University (~1992–2002).
A scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology, Nohin studied under Gadjin Nagao and served as an assistant professor at Ryukoku University.
A specialist in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, Tsuchiya studied at Kokugakuin University (~1980–1989) and held a post at Senshu University around 2005.

Anesaki, a scholar of religion and Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Tokyo, the University of Kiel, and under Friedrich Max Müller and Paul Deussen. He was a professor at the University of Tokyo and lectured at Collège de France.

A scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology, Imai studied at Tokyo University of Education (~1961–1970). He held academic posts at Ibaraki University (~1977–1984) and the University of Tsukuba (~1984–2005).

A historian, archaeologist, and Buddhist studies scholar, Mori studied at Nagoya University and the University of London (SOAS) under Tadeusz Skorupski. He held posts at Nagoya University, Koyasan University, and Kanazawa University.
Specializing in Buddhist studies, Asada studied at Ryukoku University (~1964–1973) and served there as an assistant professor around 1987.
